title: Art Direction for AAA UI
abstracted_dimensions: shape primitives as a visual-language foundation
negative space as part of shape language

legibility under functional display constraints
limitations: the source addresses interface art direction rather than faction, magic, or technology illustration directly

mechanisms.statement: shape vocabulary assigns a small set of contour primitives and negative-space rhythms to each system before ornament is added
color and value roles encode affiliation, function, and hazard only when repeated across objects, effects, and environments
effect timing, direction, origin, and dissipation distinguish activation, impact, sustain, and recovery states
material families encode construction culture through shared roughness, pattern, aging, and repair logic while allowing local variation
joint, fastening, seam, and energy-transfer rules make technology or magic appear built and operable rather than decorative
system identity survives object-scale changes when silhouette, material, and effect cues share a hierarchy
faction differentiation needs both within-system coherence and between-system contrast on at least two visible axes
exceptions become narrative evidence only after the base visual system is established and the deviation has a visible cause

illustration_evidence_definitions.system_shape_vocabulary: Two or three recurring contour primitives visibly organize architecture, equipment, costume hardware, and effects without relying on an emblem.
illustration_evidence_definitions.system_negative_space_rhythm: Openings, gaps, cutouts, and spacing repeat a recognizable proportion and direction across unrelated system assets.
illustration_evidence_definitions.system_material_family: A bounded set of surface classes repeats with visibly consistent roughness, reflectance, grain scale, and fabrication logic.
illustration_evidence_definitions.system_construction_joint_rule: Seams, fasteners, overlaps, sockets, or conduits visibly explain how parts connect and transfer load or energy.
illustration_evidence_definitions.system_color_value_role: A limited value and color role recurs for structure, interaction, warning, and active energy rather than decorating every surface equally.
illustration_evidence_definitions.system_effect_lifecycle: One effect visibly has a source, travel direction, impact or sustain state, and residue or dissipation behavior.
illustration_evidence_definitions.system_wear_repair_logic: Damage, maintenance, replacement, and repair marks occur at plausible contact, heat, stress, or access zones.
illustration_evidence_definitions.system_rule_break_exception: One asset visibly violates an established system rule and the scene supplies a causal trace for that exception.

compatibility: combine one shape vocabulary with one material family and one construction rule before adding effect ornament
pair any active color or glow with a visible source, target, and lifecycle state
repeat at least two system cues across a character-scale object and an environment-scale object
use a rule-breaking asset only when two or more surrounding assets establish the normal rule
conflicts: do not use hue alone as proof of faction, magic type, morality, or technology level
do not mix incompatible fastening, material, and energy-transfer logics without a visible history of adaptation
do not stack every emblem, glow, engraving, particle, and rare material at equal prominence
do not treat pristine surfaces, emissive lines, or ornate geometry as universal evidence of advanced or magical function
counterexamples: several unrelated objects share one accent color but have no common silhouette, material, or construction logic
an emblem is pasted onto otherwise generic equipment and is the only affiliation cue
particles appear around an object without a source, direction, contact effect, or residue
every asset is equally pristine despite different use, exposure, and maintenance conditions
boundaries: no protected faction emblem, signature silhouette, named power effect, proprietary interface, or distinctive palette-layout combination is reproduced
living religious symbols, sacred diagrams, ceremonial objects, and real ritual procedures are not normalized as generic magic decoration
visual grammar never supplies real weapon construction, harmful engineering, or operational instructions
moral worth, ethnicity, class, or intelligence is never inferred from material cleanliness, geometry, or color
the sources support design mechanisms and production constraints, not universal viewer-preference claims
format_implications: key art should show one system cue at character scale and one at environment scale
small cards and thumbnails should preserve silhouette and value roles even when material detail disappears
monochrome manga output should translate color roles into value, pattern density, and edge hierarchy
sequential panels should keep the base grammar stable while changing effect lifecycle and damage state
cropped promotional variants should retain at least two non-emblem affiliation cues
viewer_implications: coherent systems let viewers classify unfamiliar assets before reading exposition
visible operation and wear invite prediction about use, maintenance, and history
bounded exceptions reward repeat viewing because the deviation carries story information
multi-axis differentiation reduces confusion without requiring stereotype-heavy color coding

title: What Happened Here? Environmental Storytelling
abstracted_dimensions: environmental properties interpreted as a meaningful whole
history, inhabitants, living conditions, function, mood, and future possibility
viewer association of separated clues
perception and active inference as investment
designer-authored and systemic environmental evidence
limitations: the source analyzes explorable game spaces rather than single illustrations

reuse_note: Only abstract clue, consequence, function, and inference mechanisms are reused; no named environment, level layout, scene, photograph, prop arrangement, or source wording is copied.

mechanisms.statement: cohesive environmental properties let separate clues be interpreted as one meaningful event or condition
arranged objects can show the final outcome of a sequence and invite viewers to infer the missing cause
functional zones, access paths, storage, and scale cues communicate who uses a place and what work occurs there
wear, repair, accumulation, and displacement map repeated use and change over time
absence becomes legible through interrupted routines, unused capacity, and objects positioned for someone no longer present
a familiar functional anchor makes one anomalous detail easier to notice and interpret
detail hierarchy should reserve the strongest contrast and density for a small number of diagnostic clue clusters
background evidence should be causally constrained yet leave enough uncertainty for viewer participation

illustration_evidence_definitions.lived_in_task_cluster: Three or fewer objects are arranged at reachable distances around one unfinished or recently completed task.
illustration_evidence_definitions.lived_in_path_wear: Repeated travel or handling is visible through compressed, polished, dirty, faded, or displaced surfaces along a plausible route.
illustration_evidence_definitions.lived_in_repair_trace: A patch, brace, replacement part, tied support, or altered seam visibly answers a prior failure while remaining usable.
illustration_evidence_definitions.lived_in_storage_logic: Tools, supplies, personal items, and waste occupy distinct accessible places that reflect frequency and sequence of use.
illustration_evidence_definitions.lived_in_cause_effect_trace: At least two spatially connected traces allow a viewer to infer an event direction from cause to consequence.
illustration_evidence_definitions.lived_in_absence_imprint: An interrupted routine, empty capacity, or prepared object visibly implies a missing participant without showing a body or written exposition.
illustration_evidence_definitions.lived_in_scale_affordance: Handle height, seat wear, step spacing, reach distance, or modified access visibly identifies the kind of user or task.
illustration_evidence_definitions.lived_in_focal_clue_hierarchy: One diagnostic clue cluster receives the highest contrast or detail, while secondary traces remain discoverable and supporting.

candidate_definitions.lived_in_background_world_evidence: Research-family router that composes routine, function, material history, and causal clues; it is not a request for generic clutter.

candidate_definitions.lived_in_path_wear: Runtime atom requiring repeated-use traces aligned to a plausible movement or handling path.
candidate_definitions.lived_in_repair_trace: Runtime atom requiring a visible repair that answers a specific functional failure.
candidate_definitions.lived_in_storage_logic: Runtime atom separating frequently used, reserved, personal, and discarded objects by access logic.
candidate_definitions.lived_in_cause_effect_trace: Runtime atom requiring two or more connected traces with an inferable event direction.
candidate_definitions.lived_in_absence_imprint: Runtime atom implying a missing participant through interrupted routine or prepared capacity rather than exposition.
candidate_definitions.lived_in_scale_affordance: Runtime atom using reach, height, spacing, wear, or adaptation to identify user and function.
candidate_definitions.lived_in_focal_clue_hierarchy: Runtime atom assigning primary contrast to one diagnostic clue cluster and lower contrast to supporting traces.

compatibility: pair a task cluster with storage logic so the scene shows both current action and repeated routine
combine path wear with a repair trace when the setting should reveal long-term adaptation
use one familiar functional anchor beside one causally connected anomaly
place a primary clue in high contrast and keep two secondary traces discoverable at closer inspection
conflicts: do not substitute random clutter, dirt, or ruin density for lived history
do not place wear uniformly on every edge and surface regardless of contact or access
do not combine several catastrophic causes whose directions and material consequences contradict each other
do not let decorative background detail compete equally with the character action and primary clue
counterexamples: a room contains many objects but none are reachable, grouped by task, stored, worn, or causally related
every object is distressed with the same scratch and grime pattern
a broken door, spilled liquid, burn mark, and overturned furniture imply incompatible event directions
written lore labels explain the setting while visible objects provide no functional or historical evidence
boundaries: no protected set layout, signature prop tableau, distinctive room geometry, readable lore document, or copied scene is reproduced
real disasters, death scenes, displacement, poverty, and sacred sites are not aestheticized as generic ruin texture
personal photographs, addresses, records, names, and other identifying details are excluded from environmental clues
accessibility adaptations are treated as ordinary lived infrastructure, never as evidence of tragedy or deficiency
the sources support practitioner design heuristics and inference opportunities, not universal or deterministic viewer readings
format_implications: single illustrations need a primary clue visible at first glance and secondary traces available on closer viewing
wide key art can distribute cause and consequence across foreground, middle ground, and background
small thumbnails should preserve the task cluster and primary anomaly even when surface wear disappears
sequential panels can reveal clues progressively without changing their causal geometry
character-centered covers should let background evidence support the promise rather than become an equal-detail inventory
viewer_implications: causal traces let viewers participate by reconstructing what happened instead of receiving exposition
routine and repair cues support attachment by implying ordinary lives beyond the depicted moment
a familiar anchor lowers interpretive load while one anomaly creates curiosity
layered clue hierarchy can reward repeat viewing without making the first read incoherent

mechanisms.statement: canonical front, side, three-quarter, and back views establish proportion and construction invariants before dramatic posing
expression and action sheets sample allowable deformation so continuity does not freeze the character into one neutral pose
identity anchors should persist across lighting, camera, outfit, expression, and environment changes

illustration_evidence_definitions.identity_canonical_turnaround: A neutral-scale reference shows front, side, three-quarter, and back views aligned to the same height and construction landmarks.
illustration_evidence_definitions.identity_proportion_landmarks: A small set of stable ratios and attachment points visibly aligns head, torso, limbs, costume breaks, and major accessories across views.
illustration_evidence_definitions.identity_face_feature_anchor: Two or more non-protected facial relationships such as spacing, contour break, or marking placement remain stable across angle and expression.
illustration_evidence_definitions.identity_silhouette_anchor: At least one head, torso, garment, or accessory contour remains recognizable when internal detail is removed.
illustration_evidence_definitions.identity_palette_material_anchor: A bounded value grouping and material assignment remains stable even when lighting and local color shift.
illustration_evidence_definitions.identity_expression_range_sheet: A reference row shows neutral and several distinct expressions while preserving construction landmarks and documenting intentional deformation.
illustration_evidence_definitions.identity_state_delta_log: Each outfit, damage, transformation, or time state lists what changes, what persists, and what visible cause connects the states.
illustration_evidence_definitions.identity_cross_scene_holdout: The same original character remains recognizable in a new camera angle, lighting condition, action, and environment not used in the canonical sheet.

candidate_definitions.identity_proportion_landmarks: Runtime atom fixing a small set of construction ratios and attachment points across views.
candidate_definitions.identity_face_feature_anchor: Runtime atom preserving two or more facial spatial relationships across angle and expression.
candidate_definitions.identity_silhouette_anchor: Runtime atom preserving at least one distinctive generic contour under detail removal.
candidate_definitions.identity_palette_material_anchor: Runtime atom preserving bounded value grouping and material assignment under changed lighting.

compatibility: pair the canonical turnaround with an expression range so construction and expressivity are both specified
keep at least three identity anchors while changing no more state features than the narrative requires
pair every damaged or transformed state with a delta log and one visible causal trace
evaluate a cross-scene holdout separately for identity, action, environment, and style
conflicts: do not lock every pose to the neutral turnaround until gesture and emotional range disappear
do not change face spacing, silhouette, palette assignment, costume breaks, and signature object all at once without declaring a new identity
do not use identical framing and expression as the only evidence of continuity
do not treat stable rendering style as proof that character identity or story state is correct
counterexamples: a portrait grid repeats the same camera angle but drifts when the character turns
the face stays similar while costume structure, scale, markings, and carried object change randomly
all views are visually consistent because they reuse one rigid neutral pose with no expression or action range
a later damaged state adds decorative scratches that do not align with any event, material, or prior panel
boundaries: no protected character turnaround, distinctive costume construction, signature prop, facial marking system, palette, or model sheet is copied
identity is not inferred from race, gender presentation, disability, body size, or other demographic stereotype
proportion landmarks are character-specific design controls, never ideals for human bodies
automated similarity metrics are supporting evidence and cannot replace direct review of action, state, and recognizable identity
the sources span training practice and generative evaluation but do not prove one universal minimum number of views or anchors
format_implications: manga and webtoon sequences need stable anchors across close-up, medium, and full-body panels
key art variants can change pose and camera while retaining silhouette, value, and material anchors
collectible cards should treat costume and damage as typed states rather than independent redraws
animation or motion references need expression and action extremes beyond orthographic views
small avatars require a reduced anchor subset tested separately from full-resolution art
viewer_implications: stable anchors reduce the effort required to identify a character after cuts and state changes
controlled variation makes growth, damage, disguise, and transformation readable as story rather than generation drift
separate continuity dimensions help preserve emotional performance instead of rewarding rigid repetition
holdout scenes expose whether recognition depends on one memorized pose or survives genuine narrative variation

title: Judging a Book by Its Cover
abstracted_dimensions: cover as an implicit signaling system

limitations: the study covers a bounded set of fiction genres and experienced readers

mechanisms.statement: a cover acts as a learned promise between publisher and experienced reader, not a universal dictionary of genre symbols
the promise should prioritize protagonist, relationship, central tension, or world hook through hierarchy instead of stacking stereotype tokens
one dominant visual proposition and one secondary reveal create a clearer first read than several equal claims
gaze measures can reveal what receives attention, but fixation or dwell alone does not establish liking, comprehension, or purchase
title, author, and imprint regions should be planned as compositional negative space before illustration detail is committed
critical faces, gestures, silhouettes, and world hooks need crop resilience inside trim and text-safe regions
thumbnail evaluation should preserve value grouping, focal hierarchy, and the primary promise after fine detail and text become unreadable
a series cover can retain a shared visual grammar while giving each volume one narratively meaningful delta

illustration_evidence_definitions.cover_primary_promise: One immediately legible character action, relationship, dilemma, or world event carries the cover's first-read proposition.
illustration_evidence_definitions.cover_character_relation_hierarchy: Scale, overlap, gaze, gesture, and distance visibly assign primary and supporting relationship roles without requiring labels.
illustration_evidence_definitions.cover_world_hook: One original object, environmental rule, or causal anomaly visibly distinguishes the setting from a generic genre backdrop.
illustration_evidence_definitions.cover_secondary_reveal: A lower-contrast clue adds a second interpretation after the primary promise is understood.
illustration_evidence_definitions.cover_title_safe_negative_space: A bounded low-detail region is reserved for later human typography without covering faces, hands, primary action, or the world hook.
illustration_evidence_definitions.cover_crop_resilient_silhouette: The primary figure and action remain identifiable when outside bleed, spine, banner, or platform crop regions are removed.
illustration_evidence_definitions.cover_thumbnail_value_group: Two or three large value masses preserve focal hierarchy when the cover is reduced until texture and small text disappear.
illustration_evidence_definitions.cover_series_delta_anchor: A recurring layout or motif system remains stable while one visible action, relationship, state, or world clue changes for the current volume.

candidate_definitions.cover_world_hook: Runtime atom requiring one original object, rule, or causal anomaly that differentiates the setting.

compatibility: combine one primary promise with at most one secondary reveal and one world hook
reserve title-safe negative space before finalizing hair, hands, effects, and background detail
use gaze, gesture, overlap, and scale together when a relationship is the promise
retain one series anchor while changing one action, relationship, state, or world consequence per volume
conflicts: do not stack crowns, weapons, flowers, school architecture, magical circles, interface panels, and decorative borders merely to announce genre
do not assign equal contrast, scale, and detail to several unrelated characters and hooks
do not place critical faces, hands, or causal clues under expected title, spine, trim, or platform crop regions
do not ask the image model to render final readable title typography as part of the illustration grammar
counterexamples: a dense inventory of familiar genre objects communicates category but no specific story promise
a polished character portrait shows no relationship, dilemma, action, or distinctive world rule
the full-resolution art is readable but the primary figure merges into the background at thumbnail size

boundaries: no protected cover composition, proprietary series lockup, publisher mark, title treatment, character design, or distinctive motif arrangement is reproduced
genre signals are learned and market-dependent; they are never treated as universal or mandatory stereotypes
eye attention is not reported as proof of purchase intent, preference, comprehension, or commercial success
typography, localization, imprint placement, and final print preflight remain downstream human design tasks
right-to-left and left-to-right markets require explicit layout direction rather than an assumed universal reading path
format_implications: print covers need bleed, trim, spine, barcode, and text-safe overlays before illustration approval

viewer_implications: a clear promise helps the intended reader decide whether the story relationship or tension merits closer inspection

crop and thumbnail resilience protect emotional and narrative cues in crowded commercial browsing contexts
